newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong committed to free trade - official.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong committed to free trade - official.

text.p: Hong Kong's commitment to free trade and a policy of minimum intervention and maximum support will remain in force after the handover to China on July 1, the territory's top trade official said on Thursday.
"We are totally committed to free trade," Alan Lai, director general of trade, told a business audience.
"No tariffs, no restrictions and no exceptions. We don't pick winners, target industries or protect and subsidise."
Hong Kong, which is to become a Special Administrative Region of China at midnight on June 30, will maintain its own customs and immigration controls, Lai said.

Free trade was just one of several elements essential to Hong Kong's continuous strategic role, including a separate legal system, autonomy in all areas except defence and foreign affairs, and the perpetuation of the territory's capitalist way of life, he added.

"Hong Kong will continue to help China tap its huge economic potential. Hong Kong will continue to play a key part in the economic development in the Asia-Pacific, the most dynamic and exciting part of the world in economic terms," Lai said.
Hong Kong has few doubts that regional initiatives spearheaded by the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum will reinforce and spur liberalisation on a larger scale, he said.
"We firmly believe that global free trade will bring maximum economic benefits to all," Lai said.
